bib.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

question: Does RLVR give LLMs reasoning abilities beyond the base model, or does it only make the base model's existing reasoning paths more likely to be sampled?
hypothesis: RLVR improves sampling efficiency but the reasoning capacity of RL-trained models remains bounded by the base model, so base models should match or beat them at large pass@k.
contributions: Systematic pass@k study of base vs RLVR models across math, code and visual reasoning, several model families and RL algorithms
Accuracy-distribution, solvable-set coverage and perplexity analyses showing RLVR paths already lie in the base distribution
Sampling Efficiency Gap (delta SE) comparing six RL algorithms against the base model's pass@256
Comparison showing distillation expands the reasoning boundary while RLVR does not

method.summary: Compares pass@k (k up to 1024) of base models against released RLVR checkpoints (SimpleRLZoo, Oat-Zero, DAPO, Code-R1, DeepCoder, EasyR1) on math, code and visual benchmarks, plus own VeRL runs of six RL algorithms on Qwen2.5-7B. Adds accuracy histograms, solvable-set overlap, perplexity of RL responses under the base model, and a distilled-model comparison.
method.task: RLVR for math, code generation and visual math reasoning; evaluation of reasoning boundary with pass@k

datasets.name: GSM8K + MATH train (SimpleRLZoo training)
datasets.preprocessing: correctness reward only, no format reward

datasets.name: MATH500
datasets.split: out-of-domain test in own runs; also eval for released models, n=128

datasets.name: AIME24
datasets.preprocessing: a heuristic-filtered subset of 18 questions used for CoT check

datasets.name: AMC23, GSM8K, Minerva, Olympiad
datasets.split: n=1024 for AMC23; n=128 for GSM8K, Minerva; Olympiad n=128 Qwen, 1024 LLaMA

datasets.name: MathVista-TestMini, MathVision-TestMini
datasets.source: Lu et al. 2024; Wang et al. 2024

other.use: generated 8 responses per problem as YGT in perplexity analysis

training.objective: Own VeRL runs on Qwen2.5-7B with PPO, GRPO, Reinforce++, RLOO, ReMax, DAPO; binary verifiable reward; KL term removed
training.batch_size: prompt batch size 256, 8 responses per prompt, PPO mini-batch size 256
training.steps: GRPO checkpoints at 150, 300, 450 (n=8); n=32 run 220 steps; KL run 450 steps
training.regularisation: KL coefficient 0.001 in one ablation only; main runs have no KL
training.compute: DAPO needs about 3 to 6x more samples per batch than other algorithms

other.n_rollouts_ablation: n increased from 8 to 32 at unchanged prompt batch size
other.note: Released-checkpoint models (SimpleRLZoo, Oat-Zero, DAPO, Code-R1, DeepCoder, EasyR1, Magistral) were not trained by the authors

inference.temperature: 0.6 (main); 1.0 and 1.2 in Fig 17; matched-entropy RL temps 0.85 to 1.5 in Fig 18
inference.samples: n = largest k on each curve (128, 256 or 1024) per problem; unbiased pass@k estimator for all k<=n
inference.prompting: zero-shot, no few-shot for base models; base uses the same prompt as the RL model (or benchmark default)

parameters.n per benchmark: n=128 MATH500, Minerva, GSM8K; n=1024 AMC23, AIME24; Olympiad n=128 Qwen, 1024 LLaMA
parameters.delta_SE: RL pass@1 minus base pass@k with k=256

other.CoT validity check: manual inspection of correct CoTs on problems with average accuracy below 5%
other.AIME24 guess filter: drop problems the base answers correctly without CoT with probability below 5% but non-zero; leaves 18 of 30

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k) averaged over problems; a problem counts solved if any of k samples passes the verifier

metrics.name: Sampling efficiency gap (delta SE)
metrics.definition: RL model pass@1 minus base model pass@256

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: exp of mean negative log-likelihood of response Y given prompt x under model m

baselines: Base model of each RLVR checkpoint
eval.protocol: Single sampling run per model, n samples per problem; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported; manual CoT validity checks on small subsets

evidence.quote: we use a temperature of 0.6 and a top-p value of 0.95, allowing a maximum generation of 16,384 tokens

results.claim: Base models overtake RLVR models as k grows: on Minerva with a 32B model the base solves about 9% more problems at k=128.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-32B base vs SimpleRLZoo GRPO model, Minerva, k=128, temperature 0.6
results.quote: For example, on the Minerva benchmark with a 32B-sized model, the base model outperforms the RL-trained model by approximately 9% at k = 128, implying that it can solve around 9% more problems in the validation set.

results.claim: On AIME24 at k=1024 with SimpleRLZoo Qwen2.5-7B, 13.3% of problems are solved only by the base model and 0.0% only by the RL model.
results.metric: share of problems solved only by base
results.table: Table 2, row base check / RL cross, column AIME24: 63.3%, 13.3%, 0.0%, 23.3%

results.claim: On MATH500 at k=128, 3.6% of problems are solved only by the base model and 1.0% only by the RL model.
Training-set pass@1 under GRPO on Omni-MATH rises from 26.1 to 42.5 over training while pass@256 falls.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-7B, VeRL GRPO, Omni-MATH-Train, steps 150 to 450
results.quote: pass@1 on the training set consistently improves from 26.1 to 42.5.

results.claim: Omni-MATH-Train pass@256 falls from 67.2 (base) to 64.3 at GRPO step 450.
results.table: Table 4, row GRPO-step450, column Omni-MATH-Train pass@256; base row 67.2

results.claim: Omni-MATH-Test (in-domain) pass@256 falls from 69.1 to 63.9 by step 450 while pass@1 rises from 10.2 to 28.3.
results.table: Table 4, row GRPO-step450, column Omni-MATH-Test pass@256; base row 69.1

results.claim: Sampling efficiency gap stays above 40 points for all six RL algorithms on the in-domain test set.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-7B, VeRL, Omni-MATH-Test, delta SE = RL pass@1 minus base pass@256
results.quote: Furthermore, we observe that ∆SE remains consistently above 40 points across different algorithms
results.note: Text says 'ranging from GRPO's 43.9 to RLOO's best 42.6'; Fig 8 labels SE = 0.410 and 0.408, so the in-text range is not obviously consistent with the figure

results.claim: Distilled DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B has a pass@k curve consistently above its base Qwen2.5-Math-7B, unlike the RL model.
results.setup: Minerva, Qwen2.5-Math-7B family, k up to 128
results.quote: the pass@k curve of the distilled model is consistently and significantly above that of the base model.

results.claim: A larger rollout number n=32 improves pass@k slightly over n=8 but the RL model is still eventually outperformed by the base.
results.quote: As shown in Figure 16, pass@k improves slightly over n = 8, but the RL-trained model is still eventually outperformed by the base model.

results.claim: A KL term (0.001) gives similar pass@1 to GRPO but much lower pass@128.
results.quote: the KL-regularized model achieves similar pass@1 to GRPO without KL, but with a much lower pass@128.

results.claim: Raising the RL model's temperature to match the base's entropy narrows but does not close the gap.
results.quote: it still underperforms the base model across pass@k.

results.claim: Manual CoT check on GSM8K: base answered 25 hard problems, 24 with at least one correct CoT; RL model 25 with 23.
results.setup: GSM8K problems with average accuracy above 0% and below 5%
results.quote: The base model answered 25 such questions, with 24 containing at least one correct CoT.

results.claim: Code and visual-reasoning results follow the math pattern; DeepCoder-14B tested only on LiveCodeBench.
results.setup: Code-R1-Zero 7B on LiveCodeBench, HumanEval+, MBPP+; Qwen2.5-VL-7B on MathVista, MathVision
results.quote: the effects of RLVR on three code generation benchmarks exhibit trends that are highly consistent with those observed in mathematical benchmarks.

results.claim: Magistral-Medium (RLVR) solves about 7 more AIME24 and 8 more AIME25 problems at k=1, with the gap narrowing as k grows.
results.metric: extra AIME24 problems solved at k=1
results.setup: Mistral-Medium-3 vs Magistral-Medium-2506 via API, 40k context, k up to 1024
results.quote: at k = 1, the RLVR-enhanced model solves approximately 7 more problems on AIME24 and 8 more on AIME25 compared to its base version.

results.claim: DAPO needs about 3 to 6x more samples per batch than other algorithms and drops significantly at k=256.
results.quote: its dynamic sampling strategy requires approximately 3 ∼6× more samples per batch during training compared to other algorithms.

results.claim: Code-R1 evaluation reproduction: pass@1 28.6 vs reported 29.7 on LiveCodeBench.
results.quote: Using this setup, we reproduce a pass@1 score of 28.6, which is close to the reported 29.7.

limits: Only open-source pure-RLVR models were testable; many strong models and pipelines are proprietary (Section 7).
RL for LLMs evolves quickly and newer techniques may mitigate the findings (Section 7).
Whether scaling RLVR compute to pretraining scale changes the result is left open (Sections 4.4, 4.6).
Most evidence compares released checkpoints whose training recipes the authors did not control; own controlled runs are on Qwen2.5-7B with Omni-MATH only.
Single sampling run per model; no confidence intervals or seeds reported.
Math pass@k can be inflated by lucky guesses; validity was checked manually only on small subsets (25 GSM8K, 7 AIME24 problems, 8 visual problems).
DeepSeek-R1-Zero could not be evaluated for throughput reasons (Section 4.6).
Code and vision tasks start from instruction-tuned models, not true zero-RL.
